descs: Ash and black glass, gray on gray, and the smell of old smoke that never quite airs out.

spots.name: Ash Furrows
spots.desc: Wind has combed the drifted ash into long parallel furrows, though no wind blows here now to have done it. Old footprints, not recent, cross them at every angle.

spots.name: The Cinder Watch Rise
spots.desc: The ground climbs toward a broken tower, its crown just visible over the rise. North, a stair spirals up into what's left of it.
spots.brief: Rising ground. North: a broken tower.

spots.name: Glassmelt Flats
spots.desc: The ground itself went to glass here, smooth and black and faintly warm underfoot, centuries on. Your own reflection looks back at you, wrong side up.

spots.name: The Charcoal Run Verge
spots.desc: Cart-ruts run north toward a stockade of stacked cordwood and old rope. Someone up there is running charcoal past a levy that was never meant to reach this far out.

spots.name: The Sunken Kiln
spots.desc: A collapsed glass-kiln, older than any furnace Glasswick runs today, swallowed by ash to its rim. Something dried and leafy grows stubbornly in the one warm crack still breathing heat.
spots.brief: An old kiln, swallowed by ash.

spots.name: Bottle Row
spots.desc: Hundreds of blown bottles lie half-buried, warped and fused by heat into shapes no glassworker ever intended, glinting whenever the light finds them.

spots.name: The Singed Orchard
spots.desc: Dead fruit trees stand in rows, trunks glassed black at the base, upper branches gray and bare. They have kept their shape out of habit longer than any tree ought to.
spots.brief: Dead trees, glassed at the root.

spots.name: Cracked Flat
spots.desc: A wide pan of black glass, sheet-cracked into a thousand plates that shift and grind underfoot like river ice about to give.

spots.name: The Levy Cairns
spots.desc: Stone cairns mark where the Ironbound weighs charcoal carts before Glasswick ever sees a coin for them. Chalk tallies, rained half away, still cling to the nearest stone.

spots.name: The Sand Mine Verge
spots.desc: The ground opens west into an old mine-mouth, timbers sagging, dug once for the pale sand Glasswick's furnaces still crave.

spots.name: The Glass Orchard
spots.desc: More dead trees, fused mid-fall as if the heat caught them still standing. A scrap of scorched cloth flutters from one low branch, snagged there and never freed.
spots.brief: Fused trees, a scrap of cloth.

spots.name: The Ridge Foot
spots.desc: The ground rises north toward a ridge that glitters wrong in any light. Singing carries down from it, faint, unhurried, and never quite stops.
spots.brief: Rising ground. Singing, faint, from above.

variants.desc: The ground rises north toward a ridge that glitters wrong in any light. No singing carries down from it now. The quiet is stranger than the sound ever was.
The ground rises north toward a ridge that glitters wrong in any light. Singing still carries down from it, softer than it was, easier to walk under.
variants.brief: Rising ground. Singing, quieter for now.

variants.desc: The ground rises north toward a ridge that glitters wrong in any light. Singing carries down from it louder than it ever did before the fifth fire.
variants.brief: Rising ground. Singing, louder than before.

spots.name: The Bell-Shard Flat
spots.desc: Shards of glass lie scattered in the rough curve of a bell, as if the shape itself had shattered and fallen from a great height. One piece, small and whole, has caught a child's eye before yours.

spots.name: Glasswick's Edge
spots.desc: Furnace-smoke shows east through the haze, and Glasswick's rooftops crowd the ash-line where the flats give out into a living town.

spots.name: The Slag Heaps
spots.desc: Centuries of glasswork have piled slag into low black hills, some of it still faintly warm to a bare hand, none of it worth a furnace's trouble anymore.

spots.name: Trapper's Ash
spots.desc: A hunter's blind, collapsed at one corner, aimed out over ground where nothing has moved in longer than anyone in Glasswick can say.

spots.name: The Long Melt
spots.desc: A river of glass runs down a shallow grade, frozen mid-flow, caught the instant it stopped running and never once since.

spots.name: Cinder Roost
spots.desc: Carrion-birds have taken a glass-cased dead tree for a roost, screaming at nothing in particular. Their droppings are the only white thing in sight.

spots.name: The Last Furrow
spots.desc: The ash gives out at last into ordinary scrub, close enough to the town that a bell rung in Glasswick carries here clean, on a still evening.

spots.name: The Burnt Milestone
spots.desc: A stone marker leans in the drift, its carved word burned past reading. Whatever it once pointed toward, the fire took the name along with the road.
onEnterOnce: This is the hold that was burned once — or so the sayings east of here have it. From where you stand, it looks less like a story and more like a very long, very patient scar.

spots.name: The Glazed Cairn Rise
spots.desc: A low mound breaks the flat, glass-slicked along one flank. South, a barrow-mouth shows dark in the slick, doorstone standing open.

spots.name: The Watching Stone
spots.desc: A flat standing stone, ash-scoured smooth, faces back toward the ridge as if someone set it there on purpose, to have something to watch from.

spots.name: Furnace Bones
spots.desc: The iron bones of a much older furnace lie half-sunk, bigger than anything Glasswick runs today and cold for longer than anyone remembers lighting it.

onEnter: Ash gathers itself into a shape too deliberate for wind, glass for teeth, and a smell like scorched sugar-sand a breath before it moves.

vars.NAME: the Glazed Cairn
vars.SIGN: Glass has run into every seam of the doorstone, as if the mound itself half-melted and set again.

vars.NAME: the Cinder Watch
vars.VIEW: the whole ash valley spreads below, Glasswick's furnace-smoke rising south and the roofless chapel white with old ash on the ridge north
vars.SIGN: An empty bell-frame still stands at the parapet, rung for the last time long ago.

vars.NAME: the Sand Mine
vars.SIGN: Sand gone to sheet glass fills the lower cuts, as if the fire found this deep before the diggers ever did.

vars.NAME: the Charcoal Run
vars.SIGN: Charcoal sacks are stacked and rope-lashed for a run past the levy road before dawn.

em_ashbalm.name: a fistful of ashbalm leaves
em_ashbalm.hint: eat it to ease a wound

fx: Bitter and warm going down, like swallowed embers. It eases the ache all the same.

em_lost_token.name: a scorched cloth token
em_lost_token.hint: Neave, at Ash Row in Glasswick, would want to know this was found

em_pip_keepsake.name: a whole bell-shaped glass shard
em_pip_keepsake.hint: Pip, at Ash Row, dared you to bring one back unbroken

em_wraith_glass.name: a shard of warm black glass
em_wraith_glass.hint: still faintly warm, however long it's been

em_cairn_castoff.name: a rust-seized digging iron
em_cairn_castoff.hint: left behind by whoever tried this barrow before you, and didn't finish

em_watch_castoff.name: a corroded bell-key
em_watch_castoff.hint: fits no bell anyone in Glasswick still owns

em_sandmine_castoff.name: a cracked glass lamp
em_sandmine_castoff.hint: the wick's long gone; the glass still holds its shape

em_cairn_ossa.name: Ossa
em_cairn_ossa.desc: A Barrow-Keeper adherent, cross-legged in the doorstone's shadow, close enough to the dark to mind it and no closer.

topics.label: who keeps watch here
topics.say: Ossa. A Keeper, for what that's worth this close to Glasswick's fire. Someone should sit with the mound, even if none of us will go past what's guarding it.

topics.label: ask her plainly what's owed here
topics.say: You want to know what a barrow owes the living. Nothing. It's what the living still owe it that keeps me sitting on this cold stone.

topics.label: offer to stand her watch a while
topics.say: She looks at you a long moment, then makes room without a word. Between the two of you, the cold at the mound's mouth is almost bearable.

em_cinderrun_hurn.name: Hurn
em_cinderrun_hurn.desc: A charcoal-runner posted to the stakes, counting sacks under his breath and losing the count every time you're in earshot.

topics.label: why he's out at the stakes
topics.say: Hurn. Dray's got me watching the gap till the last sacks are counted. Long as you're not levy folk, I've got no quarrel with you standing here.

topics.label: ask what the run's really carrying
topics.say: More than charcoal, if you're asking right. He says it slow, watching you the whole time, like the answer costs him something to give away free.

topics.label: size up the stakes with a soldier's eye
topics.say: You name the gap Hurn's been paid to mind without being told where it is. He goes a shade paler and starts watching it instead of you.

em_wraith.name: glass-ash wraith
em_wraith.desc: Ash held together in roughly a man's shape, glass shards for teeth and fingers, moving like something still deciding how joints work.
onDeath: It comes apart into ash and loose glass before it finishes falling, no body left to speak of. One shard keeps enough shape to pocket.
